summary: Kaj Barr was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Den Polytekniske Læreanstalt, University of Copenhagen under Christensen and Tuxen, and University of Göttingen under Andreas. He later taught at Copenhagen, succeeding Christensen in 1945.

Kakichi Kadowaki was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1948 to 1951, studied under Sogen Omori, and served on the faculty at Sophia University from ~1965 to 1997.
Kakushō Ujiie was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied abroad at Tribhuvan University. He later served as a professor at Koyasan University, attested in 1970 and 1984–1985.

Kali Kinkar Datta was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute as honorary director (attested 1959–1966) and joint director (attested 1987), and as vice-chancellor of Patna University (attested 1973).

Kalidas Nag was an Indologist and historian who studied at Scottish Church College, University of Calcutta, and under Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta (~1923–1955), and The Asiatic Society (~1942–1946).
Kalpana K. Sheth is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani. She held an academic post at the L.D. Institute of Indology.
Kalpana Ram is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the Australian National University between 1981 and 1989, where she was also attested in a post in 2026.

Kalu Rinpoche worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Ösel Ling under teachers including Norbu Tondrup, Khakyab Dorje, and Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, serving as Palpung's Vajra Master and abbot of Changchub Choeling.
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served as an emeritus professor at the University of Windsor, attested in 2002.
Kamal K. Sridhar is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She held positions at Stony Brook University, serving as director (attested in 2007) and later as Professor Emerita (attested in 2026).

Kamala Tiyavanich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.

Kamaleswar Bhattacharya was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. During his career, he held academic posts at Brown University (~1968–1969), the University of Toronto (~1969–1970), and the University of Bonn.

Kameshwar Nath Mishra is an Indologist, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1982–1988, 2001) and was a visiting research scholar at the University of Marburg in 1993.

Kamil Václav Zvelebil was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný and Oldřich Friš. He held posts at the Oriental Institute, Charles University, and Utrecht University (~1977–1992).

Kamla Chowdhry studied at Santiniketan, the University of the Punjab, the University of Calcutta, and Michigan State University. She later held academic posts at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (~1962–1972) and Harvard University.

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, chairman of Kalidasa Sanskrit Academy, and advisor at Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Kammie Takahashi is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano and Paul Groner, later holding a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.
Kan Hang is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Su Bai. He has served as dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune and studied under Sukumar Sengupta, later serving as Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta.
Kanchu Onoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as a teacher at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).
